prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity native Android TV HOME SCREEN design preview, a straight-on 16:9 1920x1080 screenshot filling the entire image. No television bezel, no room, no perspective, no marketing poster. The product is a custom lightweight launcher provisionally named Luma: combine the restrained efficient native app tiles of Rivi, the tasteful depth and subtle glass panels of PLUI, and the useful content recommendations of stock Google TV. This must be a beautiful practical D-pad interface at couch viewing distance. Keep typography crisp, restrained and large enough, clean contemporary humanist sans. Colors: near-black olive charcoal #111713, warm off-white #F4F1E9, subtle muted sage #9FAF9C. Static translucent dark panels with very restrained thin edges, no neon glow, no flashy backgrounds or busy widgets. Selected control has one thin warm ivory rounded focus outline, all other controls remain calm. Only one selected control. Comfortable 5% screen-safe margins. Show real app names in accurate branded rectangular tiles: Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Disney+, Apple TV, Max. Use these same fictional sample shows with excellent cinematic poster photography in all previews: Northbound (lonely red train in alpine forest at blue hour), Night Shift (woman investigator in rainy city), Wild Coast (dramatic sunlit ocean cliffs), Orbit (astronaut against planet horizon). These are fictional examples, not the user's viewing history. Include the exact small footer text 'Example shows · Design preview'. Show a clock '8:42 PM' and simple native search/settings line icons, no FPS numbers or performance claims. Render only the actual interface, no explanation text, option letters, design notes, or headings above the screen. Structure and exact labels for this variant follow. Variant QUIET. No giant featured image. Use a static dark olive charcoal background with subtle depth only, no wallpaper texture. A slim left rail with Home, Apps, Inputs and Settings icons and understated labels. Main area starts with 'Home' at upper left and clock at upper right. The first useful row is 'Your apps': six large beautiful 16:9 app tiles with generous spacing and excellent brand marks, Netflix has the sole ivory selection outline, label 'Netflix' beneath it. The center row is 'Continue watching' with four generous cinematic landscape cards for the four fictional shows, title, provider, episode and remaining time visible below each; thin progress bars. The lower section 'Suggestions for you' shows four smaller landscape cards with different views of those fictional series, each with title and provider. Everything is flat enough to implement with cached static artwork, yet refined through proportion, spacing, gentle panel fills and typography. App row roughly 26% of usable height, Continue Watching 32%, Suggestions 25%. Avoid dense widgets, giant unused gaps and visually bland placeholder cards. Clearly denser and more direct than a cinema hero.
